title: InferenceForge: agents optimizing agentic serving
authors: Jesse Cai, Huimin Zeng, Yuxuan Lu, Dakuo Wang, Kai-Wei Chang
gist: An off-the-shelf coding agent, placed in a custom environment with a harness and an evaluation suite, tuned SGLang for Kimi K3 under a floor on per-user speed. In nine iterations over three days it found three kernel-level fixes specific to agent traffic, where a few very long contexts share a batch with many short ones, and landed them as pull requests in a fork.
changes: The first public case of outsiders with no production traffic topping the shared scoreboard using a general-purpose agent. The fixes are new code, not configuration, and each targets a traffic shape that uniform benchmarks never produce.
caveats: Measured by the authors on one node. The comparison is against runs published by other teams on other dates, not a same-day rerun. The fixes sit in a personal fork, not upstream. The cost of the agent runs is not given.

bears_on.note: A general coding agent found and validated three kernel fixes, bit-exact where claimed.
All three fixes exist only because agent traffic mixes very long and short contexts in one batch.
A public replayable workload stood in for private traffic. Outsiders could play, which weakens the idea that only traffic owners can evaluate.
States a plan to put the authors' own models, post-trained for optimisation, into the loop. A plan, not a result.
On the newest model the lead over the best public run is 5%. The public frontier is close behind.
